co_07_back_to_the_future.blurb: A steep limestone wall on the north side of The Bank at Shelf Road, outside Cañon City. It holds sixteen mostly sport lines with a few trad-style ones mixed in, and the character is technical face climbing on crimps and pockets. Grades run from the high 5.8s up to the low 5.13s, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so this is a place for strong leaders rather than beginners. The wall sits between Surreal Estate and Lesser of Two Evils, and The Bank as a whole is among the busiest parts of the canyon, so expect company on good days.
co_07_back_to_the_future.parking_note: Leave the car in the day-use lot outside The Bank campground, not along the road, and walk from there.
co_07_back_to_the_future.approach: Follow the dirt road up from the lot past 2150 Wall and the Piggy Bank, then continue along the base of the cliff to this wall. Expect a short walk of several minutes.

co_beach_the_2.blurb: A compact sport crag at the west end of The Narrows in Poudre Canyon, west of Fort Collins. All sixteen routes are bolted, and they lean hard: mostly 5.12 and 5.13 with a handful touching 5.14 and a couple at 5.11, so it suits strong climbers looking for bouldery, powerful moves with little pump. There is no easy warm-up here. The cliff catches sun early and goes into shade by late morning, and the river lies between the road and the wall.

co_big_ass_boulder.blurb: One large, nearly square sandstone block, around twenty feet tall, among the Wolcott boulders beside the Eagle River near I-70. Sixteen problems cover the whole block, from very easy ones up to a couple of hard testpieces, with most falling in the lower V grades. Some lines are highballs, and a traverse of the block is possible. The walk-in is only a few steps from where you park, which makes it a quick stop on an I-70 trip.

co_chicken_rock.blurb: The namesake cliff of the Valley of the Chickens on Badger Flats in South Park, near Lake George, at roughly 9,200 feet. Granite studded with chickenheads gives sport and trad lines of one to three pitches, from easy 5.6 terrain up to a single route in the 5.11 range, so there is plenty here for newer leaders. Gear goes in cracks and slings around the knobs, with a few bolted faces. Approaches are short and the crag is rarely busy, which makes it a pleasant quiet option away from the Front Range crowds.

co_narrows_redstone_mcclure_pass.blurb: A scattering of ice and mixed flows along the Crystal River valley near Redstone, between the Narrows and Marble. The sixteen climbs are mostly water ice, centred on WI4 with a few easier lines and several WI5s, plus some mixed pitches; typical outings are two or three pitches. Because the valley is low and sunny, the ice is fickle and most of it only forms after a heavy snow year followed by freeze-thaw cycles. Treat it as a conditions-dependent objective, and ask locals what is in before driving in.

co_cascade_creek.blurb: A winter canyon on Highway 550 north of Durango, just past Purgatory and below Coal Bank Summit, at about 8,700 feet. Frozen waterfalls drop around a pool beneath limestone walls, with reliable ice on the south side and steeper, harder mixed lines on the north. Ice here spans roughly WI4 to WI6, and the mixed routes run from about M6 to M9. The main flows can get busy, and you will likely meet local ice climbers. The canyon is also a summer rock destination.
